title: Local quasi-finiteness of a locally finite type pseudo-torsor
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$, and let $G$ and $X$ be algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Suppose $G$ is a group algebraic space: multiplication $m:G\times_B G\to G$, identity $e:B\to G$ and inversion $i:G\to G$ induce group structures on $G(T)$ natural in every scheme $T\to B$. Let $a:G\times_B X\to X$ be an action, satisfying $a(gh,x)=a(g,a(h,x))$ and $a(e,x)=x$ on all test schemes. Assume the morphism
$$G\times_B X\longrightarrow X\times_B X,\qquad(g,x)\longmapsto(a(g,x),x)$$
is an isomorphism; this defines a pseudo $G$-torsor and imposes no surjectivity on $X\to B$. Suppose $G\to B$ and $X\to B$ are locally of finite type and $G\to B$ is locally quasi-finite. Then $X\to B$ is locally quasi-finite. Local finite type and local quasi-finiteness of algebraic-space morphisms mean the corresponding scheme properties [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, pqf-def-quasifinite] on etale scheme charts of source and target.

source.place: Tag 0DSK (lemma-pseudo-torsor-implications), part (2); pseudo torsor is Tag 04TW (definition-pseudo-torsor).

proof.text: Fix an etale scheme chart $V\to B$ and set $F=X\times_B V$. By the chartwise local finite type hypothesis, $h:F\to V$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open] to obtain its quasi-finite locus $Q_h\subseteq|F|$; its inverse image under any scheme base change $V'\to V$ is exactly the quasi-finite locus of $F\times_VV'\to V'$. We show every point of $|F|$ lies in $Q_h$.

source.place: Tag 0DSK (lemma-pseudo-torsor-implications), proof of (2), using the quasi-finite locus as in spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0ABM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite-locus); the scheme-target version is Tag 04NW (lemma-locally-finite-type-quasi-finite-part).

proof.text: For $z\in|F|$, choose a representative $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to F$ as in [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], and use its composite to $V$ for base change. Form $P=F\times_V\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $H=G\times_B\operatorname{Spec}K$, algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The pair $(x,1)$ is a section $x_K$ of $P\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and represents a point $z_K$ mapping to $z$. The given pseudo-torsor isomorphism pulls back to $\theta_K:H\times_KP\xrightarrow{\sim}P\times_KP$ by the fibre-product universal property. Pull it back further along $P\to P\times_KP$, $y\mapsto(y,x_K)$. Its source becomes $H$: a pair $(g,u)$ above $(y,x_K)$ must satisfy $u=x_K$ and $y=a(g,x_K)$. Thus the resulting isomorphism is $t:H\xrightarrow{\sim}P$, $g\mapsto a(g,x_K)$. Explicitly its inverse sends $y$ to the first component of $\theta_K^{-1}(y,x_K)$; both inverse identities follow from those of $\theta_K$.

source.place: Tag 0DSK (lemma-pseudo-torsor-implications), proof of (2), using the quasi-finite locus as in spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0ABM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite-locus); the scheme-target version is Tag 04NW (lemma-locally-finite-type-quasi-finite-part).

proof.text: By the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-representable-lqf-calculus-descent], $H\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally quasi-finite, since $G\to B$ is. This clause applies to algebraic-space morphisms: their scheme base changes are algebraic spaces. For any etale scheme chart $U\to P$, composing with $t^{-1}$ gives an etale chart $U\to H$ (the scheme tests are identified by the isomorphism, as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]); its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the same morphism. Hence $P\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally quasi-finite.

source.place: Tag 0DSK (lemma-pseudo-torsor-implications), proof of (2), using the quasi-finite locus as in spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0ABM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite-locus); the scheme-target version is Tag 04NW (lemma-locally-finite-type-quasi-finite-part).

proof.text: The quasi-finite locus of $P\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is all of $|P|$, by its chartwise definition. In particular it contains $z_K$. By the base-change equality in [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open], $z_K$ belongs to the inverse image of $Q_h$, so $z\in Q_h$. As $z$ was arbitrary, $Q_h=|F|$. Every etale scheme chart $U\to F$ is therefore quasi-finite over $V$ at every point, which is local quasi-finiteness by [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Since $V\to B$ was arbitrary, this is the required chartwise local quasi-finiteness of $X\to B$. If $|F|$ is empty the same argument is vacuous and all chart point conditions hold.
